messages.content: "Can you plot two sine waves for me? The first one should have a frequency of 5 Hz, starting from 0 radians and ending at 10 radians, with an amplitude of 2 and a phase shift of 1 radian. The second one should have a frequency of 10 Hz, starting from 0 radians and ending at 20 radians, with an amplitude of 3 and a phase shift of 2 radians."

function.name: plot_sine_wave
function.description: Plot a sine wave for a given frequency in a given range. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_range.description: Start of the range in radians.

end_range.description: End of the range in radians.

frequency.description: Frequency of the sine wave in Hz.

amplitude.description: Amplitude of the sine wave. Default is 1.

phase_shift.description: Phase shift of the sine wave in radians. Default is 0.

But the function signature only allows one sine wave at a time. We need to call the function twice, once for each wave. We need to call the function twice. The tool invocation format: we need to produce a JSON object with "name": "plot_sine_wave", "arguments": { ... }.

We need to do two calls. According to guidelines, we can only call one tool at a time. But we can chain calls. So we will call the tool for the first wave, then after receiving the result, call again for the second wave. But we might also combine them into separate calls. The user wants both plotted. We can call the tool twice. The first call: name: plot_sine_wave, arguments: { start_range: 0, end_range: 10, frequency: 5, amplitude: 2, phase_shift: 1 }. Then we wait for the tool response. Then we call again: name: plot_sine_wave, arguments: { start_range: 0, end_range: 20, frequency: 10, amplitude: 3, phase_shift: 2 }.

We need to produce the tool invocation. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we will produce the first tool invocation.
